patients.summary: Self-employed landscaper who joins in 2019 with peptic ulcer disease on pantoprazole, develops hypertension that becomes resistant with hypokalemia, and is found to have primary aldosteronism. A functioning pancreatic VIPoma is found in 2024 and resected; a vomiting ED visit in 2025 and a basilar tip aneurysm rupture in 2026 follow, with spironolactone finally added at her last visit.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish care with us. Previous PCP retired and the office closed out its panel. Works for herself doing landscaping, prefers early morning appts before she heads out to job sites. Booked new pt physical 4/9 at 7:40. Release form emailed for her old records. Membership info and fee schedule sent.

conditions.label: Peptic ulcer disease
conditions.note: per patient and prior office; on daily PPI since

medications.drug: pantoprazole 40 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily before breakfast

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
41F here to establish care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

Concerns: none really. Feels well. Works outdoors all season, slower in winter.

PMH: peptic ulcer disease about 7 yrs ago, treated at her old office; has stayed on pantoprazole 40 daily since and doesn't want to come off it ("every time I tried, the burning came back"). Diagnostic laparoscopy at 32 for abdominal pain, nothing found.
Meds: pantoprazole 40 mg daily. No OTC NSAIDs - was told to avoid after the ulcer.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father HTN, died after a ruptured brain aneurysm at 67. Mother T2DM and high cholesterol. Paternal aunt has an adrenal problem causing high BP - pt thinks it was called hyperaldosteronism.
SHx: self-employed landscaper/horticulturist, runs a small crew in season. Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a month. Exercises through work.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap "a few years ago," normal. No mammogram yet.

ROS: no headaches, chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, abdominal pain, change in bowels, melena. Otherwise negative.

Exam: BP above, repeated after rest similar. Pleasant, fit-appearing, tanned forearms. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopy port scars. No edema. Skin: no concerning lesions on sun-exposed areas. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap/HPV collected. Breasts: no masses bilaterally.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: Pap/HPV done. Screening mammogram ordered. Tdap today. CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH, A1c. One-time HCV and HIV screening, discussed and agreed.
2. BP borderline today. With her father's history I'd like real numbers - asked her to buy a home cuff and send readings over the next couple months. Low salt diet reviewed.
3. PUD hx - continue pantoprazole. Avoid NSAIDs.
4. FHx of ruptured aneurysm in father - noted.
RTC 1 yr, sooner for BP.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Paula - all of your bloodwork came back fine. Kidney and liver tests normal, blood count normal, cholesterol in a good range, thyroid and sugar normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Pap results will take a few more days.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap normal and HPV negative. Next one in 5 years.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Summary of care, prior internal medicine office (records released at patient request).

Patient: Paula Nowak, DOB 02/25/1978.
Problem list: peptic ulcer disease, 2012, treated, maintained on PPI.
Surgical: diagnostic laparoscopy 2010 for abdominal pain, no pathology identified.
Medications: pantoprazole 40 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Screening: Pap 2015 normal. Routine labs 2017 unremarkable.
Vitals at last visit (2017): BP 132/84.

Scanned to chart. Reviewed - consistent with her history. [PCP]

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies available for comparison. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious masses, calcifications or architectural distortion in either breast.

documents.title: Home BP
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry this is late, June was crazy. Here's what I have from the cuff, mostly mornings: 136/86, 140/88, 134/84, 142/90, 138/86, 137/88. Is that ok?

documents.title: RE: Home BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Paula. Borderline but not in treatment range yet. Keep the salt down and check a few times a month; let's look again at your next visit or if you start seeing 140s/90s regularly.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, tolerated. VIS given. BP checked at pt request, recorded. Reminded to send home readings to Dr.

documents.title: BP numbers going up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My readings have crept up this winter. Last two weeks: 150/96, 148/94, 152/98, 149/95, 151/96, 147/94. Not doing anything different. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: BP numbers going up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - those are consistently high. Front desk will set you up in the next couple of weeks. Bring the cuff so we can check it against ours.

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 74. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No ST-T abnormalities.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Home BPs running ~150/96 over the last few weeks (log in portal). Her cuff read within 3 points of ours today. No headaches, chest pain, vision change, palpitations. No NSAIDs, decongestants, licorice or supplements. Sleeping fine. Salt is moderate - eats out a lot during season, less now.

O: BP as recorded, repeated by me 148/96. Fundi not well seen without dilation. Heart RRR no murmur, no carotid bruits. Lungs clear. No edema. ECG normal, no LVH.

A/P: Hypertension, now sustained on home and office readings. Age 41, strong family hx.
- Start lisinopril 10 mg daily. Discussed cough and lip/tongue swelling as reasons to call.
- BMP and UA today, BMP again in 2 wks on the ACE.
- DASH handout, sodium under 2 g.
- Telehealth check in 3 months with home log.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and electrolytes normal; urine clean. Potassium is at the low end of normal - fine for now. Recheck in 2 weeks as planned.

documents.title: BMP on lisinopril
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine and potassium stable after starting lisinopril. Continue.

documents.title: Visit change
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Office moving routine follow-ups to video for now. Pt OK with video visit 5/14. Link sent to email on file.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her truck between jobs, identity verified. Busy spring - business is fine.
Home readings on lisinopril 10 averaging about 144/92 (14 readings sent). No cough, no swelling. Tolerating fine.
A/P: HTN improved but not at goal (<130/80). Increase lisinopril to 20 mg daily. New Rx sent; she'll finish the 10s by taking two. BMP when she is next near the office - order in. Recheck in ~4 months in person.

documents.title: Lisinopril 90-day
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy asking to convert lisinopril 20 mg to a 90-day supply per pt's insurance. Sent 90 days x 1 refill per protocol. Pantoprazole 90-day also sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
HTN f/u. Masked. On lisinopril 20 since May, says she hasn't missed doses. Home log mid-140s/low-90s. No headaches, no cough. Summer was long, lots of heat, drinking plenty of water.
Exam: BP as above both arms similar. RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
HTN - still above goal on max-ish ACE dose. Add amlodipine 5 mg daily. Ankle swelling discussed. Video check in ~10 wks.
Flu shot today.
PUD - stable on pantoprazole.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home. Off-season, doing wreaths and holiday greens out of her greenhouse.
On lisinopril 20 + amlodipine 5. Home avg ~142/92 over the past month. No ankle swelling, no flushing.
A/P: Better, still not at goal. Amlodipine up to 10 mg. If not at goal by spring will add a third agent. In-person visit March.
